item.title: West Norfolk residents honoured for wildlife-friendly gardens
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk residents honoured for wildlife-friendly gardens
West Norfolk Council has announced the winners of its second annual Garden Wildlife Competition. A ceremony held at King’s Lynn Town Hall on Tuesday celebrated residents who have transformed their outdoor spaces into havens for nature. The contest, which aims to support biodiversity, attracted 36 entries across large and small garden categories.
Winners included gardeners from Lynn, Southery, West Dereham, Great Bircham, and Downham Market. Mayor Steve Bearshaw and Councillor Michael de Whalley presented the awards, highlighting the positive impact these local habitats have on the environment. The event also featured presentations on nature recovery and the importance of supporting pollinators, encouraging further community involvement in the council’s wider biodiversity efforts.

The shop is scheduled to open this autumn to support unpaid carers across Norfolk, Cambridgeshire, and Peterborough. Shop manager Belinda Jones is now calling for more local people to join the team as the site prepares to become a community hub. item.title: Norfolk Police trial new drone technology in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk Police trial new drone technology in King’s Lynn
Norfolk Constabulary has launched a five-week trial of new "Drone as First Responder" technology. The initiative, which began on September 7, aims to provide officers with live aerial views of incidents to help direct resources more effectively. King’s Lynn is one of four areas involved in the trial, alongside Norwich, Thetford, and Great Yarmouth.
Specially trained officers will remotely pilot the drones to assist with tasks such as locating missing people, tracking suspects, and assessing developing situations. The force has confirmed that all flights will operate under strict legal frameworks and oversight. Following the trial, police will review the results to determine the potential benefits of integrating this technology into their long-term policing operations.
